## Pull request overview

Adds/updates planning documentation to benchmark ObjectStack’s visual builder UX against Airtable Interface Designer, align roadmap status with already-shipped spec work, and outline next protocol/runtime gaps to close.

**Changes:**
- Added a comprehensive UX optimization plan document with Airtable benchmark analysis and proposed schema enhancements.
- Updated the Airtable gap analysis doc to reflect Phase B completion and Phase C spec progress (plus links to the new plan).
- Updated main and Studio roadmaps + README to reference the new plan and sync Phase B/C status.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| docs/design/visual-design-ux-optimization.md | New UX optimization plan with parity matrix, gap audit, and proposed schema additions |
| docs/design/airtable-interface-gap-analysis.md | Updates status/parity claims and Phase B/C checklist progress + reference to new plan |
| apps/studio/ROADMAP.md | Adjusts Studio roadmap to emphasize runtime work and adds builder optimization initiatives |
| ROADMAP.md | Syncs Phase B/C statuses and adds link to the new optimization plan |
| README.md | Adds a reference link to the new optimization plan document |
</details>

In `InterfaceTemplateSchema`, `thumbnail` is described as an image URL but is typed as `z.string()`. In the spec, URL fields are typically validated with `z.string().url()` (e.g. many `*Url` fields across the repo). Consider updating this proposal to use URL validation to match existing schema patterns.
```suggestion
  thumbnail: z.string().url().optional().describe('Preview image URL'),
```

This Interface Builder task lists palette “12 types” including `grid`, `chart`, `details`, `list`, but these aren’t current `PageComponentType` values in the spec (e.g. the record component is `record:details`, and `grid`/`list` are page types). Clarify whether these are planned new `element:*` component types, existing page types, or correct the names to match the spec to avoid confusion for implementation.
```suggestion
| | **Airtable Interface Designer parity.** Drag-and-drop element canvas using `BlankPageLayoutSchema`. Element palette using current spec component types (initial set: text, number, image, divider, button, filter, form, record_picker, record:details, chart). Property panel per element. Snap-to-grid with alignment guides. Layer ordering. Undo/redo (50 steps). Data source binding per element (`ElementDataSourceSchema`). See `InterfaceBuilderConfigSchema` in `@objectstack/spec/studio`. | | |
```

The status line says “Phase A–C Spec Complete”, but later in Phase C the `previewAs` item is still unchecked (and the file also marks Phase C as 🟡). To avoid an internal contradiction, update the status to reflect that Phase C spec is only partially complete (or explicitly call out the remaining spec gap: `previewAs`).
```suggestion
> **Status:** Phase A–B Spec Complete · Phase C Spec In Progress (previewAs) · Studio Runtime Pending  
```

In the proposed `AlignmentToolsSchema`, `alignActions` is defined as `z.enum([...])` (a single value), but the field name/description indicate a set/list of available operations. Consider making it an array of enum values (or renaming it to singular) so the proposal matches the intended semantics.
```suggestion
  alignActions: z.array(z.enum([
    'align_left', 'align_center', 'align_right',
    'align_top', 'align_middle', 'align_bottom',
    'distribute_horizontal', 'distribute_vertical',
  ])).describe('Available alignment operations'),
```

The proposal uses a numeric `timestamp: z.number()` (“Unix timestamp”) for `BuilderHistoryEntrySchema`. Elsewhere in this repo, timestamp fields are consistently modeled as ISO 8601 strings via `z.string().datetime()`. For consistency (and easier JSON interoperability), update the proposal to use an ISO datetime string (or clearly justify why builder history is different).
```suggestion
  timestamp: z.string().datetime().describe('ISO 8601 timestamp'),
```
